proof:
# A closed planar branch: full triangular endpoint and three proper opposite cuts

This theorem concerns n=1,d=2 with exactly three positive fibers. It is
not a general OC theorem. In particular the endpoint must be the ENTIRE
canonical triangle, not an arbitrary body contained in that triangle.
The three opposite-fiber cuts must all be proper.

## 1. Statement

Let A,K be full-dimensional planar convex bodies, and set

    v_1=(1,0), v_2=(0,1), v_3=(-1,-1),
    T={x: v_i.x<=1 for i=1,2,3},       b=|T|=9/2.

Assume (A+T)/2 is contained in K. Place A,K,T at integer bases -1,0,1
respectively and use their ordinary area as mixed measure. Put

    a=|A|, k=|K|, M=a+k+b,
    U_i=|A intersect {v_i.x>=-1}|,
    q_i=|K intersect {v_i.x>=0}|.

Assume 0<U_i<a for every i and that the three actual ambient caps

    H_i={(z,x):v_i.x>=z}

have one common mass Q. Since their T traces are its facets, of area
zero, this means exactly Q=U_i+q_i for all i.

**Theorem.** If b<=M/2, then

    Q > Gamma_2 M/2 = 2M/9.                            (1)

No criticality is required for this geometric common-mass conclusion.
If, in addition, Y=(0,0) belongs to the induced mixed set and each H_i
attains its raw halfspace depth, then Y itself has the strict OC bound
whenever b<=M/2. If b>M/2, the ordinary centroid of T, at the actual
mixed point(1,0), has raw depth at least Gamma_2 b>Gamma_2 M/2. Hence
this entire explicitly stated critical-menu branch satisfies strict OC.

## 2. Ordinary three-cap profile, with its proof

If a planar convex body L is covered by three closed halfplanes with
captured areas c_1<=c_2<=c_3, then

    |L|<=c_3+c_2+c_1/4.                                (2)

Here is the needed consequence of ordinary planar Grünbaum without an
additional unproved profile theorem. More generally, for any finite
cover H_i and any alpha>=0, successively remove from the current convex
body a deeper cap inside H_i of area (current H_i mass-alpha)_+.
Continuity of cap volume supplies its threshold. Retain the opposite
closed halfplane, so convexity and compactness are preserved. Each
removal is at most (|L intersect H_i|-alpha)_+, and after all cuts each
original H_i captures at most alpha. If the remaining body has zero
area, the removal bound already proves

    |L|<=sum_i(|L intersect H_i|-alpha)_+ +alpha/Gamma_2.

Otherwise its centroid belongs to one covering H_i, and ordinary
Grünbaum bounds its area by alpha/Gamma_2, giving the same inequality.
All cutting lines are area-null; no boundary mass is removed improperly.
Set alpha=c_1 and Gamma_2=4/9 to obtain(2).

Both triples used below genuinely cover the whole plane. For the K
traces, sum_i v_i=0 prevents all three margins v_i.x from being
negative. The A traces v_i.x>=-1 also cover, since their simultaneous
strict complements would give sum_i v_i.x<-3 despite that sum being0.

## 3. A full supporting facet supplies an exact extrusion term

Let D_i=A intersect {v_i.x>=-1}, h_i=max_A v_i.x, and let
F_i=T intersect {v_i.x=1} be the FULL corresponding facet of T.
Properness of the A cut implies D_i has positive area and normal range
[-1,h_i] in the coordinate v_i.x. The facet length is

    length(F_i)=3||v_i||.

The actual midpoint relation gives

    (D_i+F_i)/2 subset K intersect {v_i.x>=0}.

In orthogonal coordinates along v_i, each slice of D_i+F_i is the
corresponding interval slice of D_i plus the same segment F_i. Their
lengths add exactly. Integrating over the normal height interval of
length (h_i+1)/||v_i|| therefore yields

    |D_i+F_i|=U_i+3(h_i+1).

Endpoint slices have height-parameter measure zero. Scaling by1/2 and
using containment proves

    q_i >=[U_i+3(h_i+1)]/4,
    4Q >=5U_i+3(h_i+1).                                (3)

This is the complete planar proof of the supporting-facet extrusion
inequality needed here. It uses no section-capacity bound, chord-centroid
condition, smoothness, or mixed-area identity. It would not be valid
with the number3 if only a smaller segment of the T facet belonged to B.

## 4. Contradiction from a putative target-sized common mass

Order the actual U_i as u<=v<=w, and define

    F=u+v+w/4.

For the K cap areas q_i=Q-U_i, formula(2) becomes

    k <= (9/4)Q-F.                                     (4)

Suppose for contradiction that Q<=2(a+b+k)/9. Combining this with(4)
gives

    k<=a+b-2F.                                         (5)

The hypothesis b<=M/2 is exactly k>=b-a. Therefore F<=a. Put

    delta=a-u-v=a-F+w/4 >=w/4>0.                        (6)

The strict positivity follows from the assumed proper positive cuts.
The strict residuals of the two caps whose areas are u and v have
intersection of area at least a-u-v=delta. Pick a point in that actual
intersection. Its two corresponding functionals are strictly below-1;
since their sum with the third functional is zero, the remaining
functional exceeds2. The remaining cap is the one of area w. Thus
its support height satisfies h_w>2. Applying(3) in that direction gives

    4Q >=5w+3(h_w+1)>5w+9,
    Q>9/4+5w/4.                                       (7)

Independently, apply(2) to the ACTUAL A cap cover. It gives

    a<=w+v+u/4,
    delta=a-u-v<=w-3u/4<=w.                            (8)

The assumed upper bound on Q and(5) give

    Q<= (4/9)(a+b-F)
      =(4/9)(b+delta-w/4)
      <=(4/9)(9/2+3w/4)
      =2+w/3.                                         (9)

But the lower quantity in(7) exceeds the upper quantity in(9) by

    1/4+11w/12>0.

This contradiction proves the STRICT inequality(1), including equality
in the nonheavy condition b=M/2. All arguments were for the same body
A and the same three ambient caps, not separately assigned mass rows.

## 5. Independent dependency audit and exact scope

The root supplied the closing chain; the two-sided agent independently
checked and wrote it in full. Each dependency is proved above except
ordinary planar Grünbaum itself. In particular:

- The A and K profiles use actual covering halfplanes, with the sorted
  orders reversed correctly in q_i=Q-U_i.
- Only B's nonheavy condition is needed; no claim about A or K being
  nonheavy is used. Strict no-heavy hypotheses are unnecessary.
- The residual intersection is a positive-area intersection of STRICT
  complements of closed A caps. Hence h_w>2 is strict, even though no
  generic position or boundary-avoidance hypothesis is imposed.
- Properness is used exactly where needed: w>0 and the captured A body's
  lower height is the cut value-1 in the extrusion computation.
- B=T supplies its actual full side of coordinate length3. An enclosing
  triangle for a smaller B does not supply this contribution.
- The source-depth conclusion is made only when the common caps are
  genuinely attaining its depth. A common-mass noncritical menu alone
  proves(1), not a lower bound for its source against unlisted caps.
- In the heavy-B alternative the selected point is the actual centroid
  in the B fiber, with ordinary Grünbaum applied to every ambient trace.
- The ambient halfspaces are the genuine coupled inequalities v_i.x>=z;
  no integer/continuous decoupling or arbitrary lattice transformation
  occurs in this normalized statement.

The residual-overlap argument eliminates the previously investigated
support-cone scalar closure in this full-T, all-proper branch. It leaves
smaller endpoint bodies, saturated opposite cuts, additional fibers,
and other dimensions outside its scope.
